headline: 7 Bangladeshis killed in Kolkata hotel fire; leaseholder arrested
summary: Two more victims from Satkhira have been identified, raising the total number of confirmed Bangladeshi deaths to seven in the devastating blaze.
details: A devastating fire at Hotel Shikha Inn in Kolkata, India, has claimed the lives of at least nine people, including seven confirmed Bangladeshi nationals.
The latest victims identified are Alimuzzaman Saju, 48, and Rebati Sarkar, 35, both residents of Kaliganj upazila in Satkhira. Both had travelled to India for medical treatment.
Other victims include a family of four from Kushtia—Debashish Dutta, Afsana Sharmin, their three-year-old son Swarnashish, and Akram Ali—along with Ahmed Babu from Savar, Dhaka.
The leaseholder of the hotel has been arrested, and two employees have been detained for questioning following the incident.
The Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata has opened a helpline (91 8274821352) to assist families of the victims.
caption:
Seven Bangladeshis have been confirmed dead after a devastating hotel fire in Kolkata.

A devastating fire at Hotel Shikha Inn in Kolkata, India, has claimed the lives of at least nine people, including seven confirmed Bangladeshi nationals.

The latest victims identified are Alimuzzaman Saju, 48, and Rebati Sarkar, 35, both residents of Kaliganj upazila in Satkhira. Both had travelled to India for medical treatment.

Other victims include a family of four from Kushtia—Debashish Dutta, Afsana Sharmin, their three-year-old son Swarnashish, and Akram Ali—along with Ahmed Babu from Savar, Dhaka.

The leaseholder of the hotel has been arrested, and two employees have been detained for questioning following the incident.

The Bangladesh Deputy High Commission in Kolkata has opened a helpline (91 8274821352) to assist families of the victims.

headline_marked: After 35 years, [[Bangladesh holds contested presidential election]] today
headline: After 35 years, Bangladesh holds contested presidential election today
summary: Members of Parliament will vote to elect the 23rd President of Bangladesh, marking the first competitive election for the post in over three decades.
details: Bangladesh is holding a presidential election today, August 20, for the first time in nearly 35 years. Voting will take place in the National Parliament from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM.

A total of 349 Members of Parliament (MPs) will cast their votes to elect the country's 23rd President. The contest is between BNP candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Ali Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance.
The voting process will involve three transparent ballot boxes placed in the parliament chamber. After voting concludes, the ballots will be counted within the chamber itself.
Chief Election Commissioner A M M Nasir Uddin will announce the results following the count. The Election Commission is expected to publish a gazette notification later today.
The newly elected President is scheduled to take the oath of office on Friday evening, August 21, at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.
This marks a historic shift, as the last contested presidential election occurred in 1991. Since then, seven consecutive presidents were elected unopposed.
caption:
For the first time in 35 years, Bangladesh is holding a contested presidential election today.

Bangladesh is holding a presidential election today, August 20, for the first time in nearly 35 years. Voting will take place in the National Parliament from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM.

A total of 349 Members of Parliament (MPs) will cast their votes to elect the country's 23rd President. The contest is between BNP candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Ali Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance.

The voting process will involve three transparent ballot boxes placed in the parliament chamber. After voting concludes, the ballots will be counted within the chamber itself.

Chief Election Commissioner A M M Nasir Uddin will announce the results following the count. The Election Commission is expected to publish a gazette notification later today.

The newly elected President is scheduled to take the oath of office on Friday evening, August 21, at the Darbar Hall of Bangabhaban.

This marks a historic shift, as the last contested presidential election occurred in 1991. Since then, seven consecutive presidents were elected unopposed.
